title: WSL Setup and Linux First Commands
description: Install Windows Subsystem for Linux and practice essential terminal commands
objective: Students will install WSL on Windows, navigate the Linux file system, create files and folders, and write their first shell script

steps.title: Install WSL
steps.instructions:
Open **PowerShell as Administrator** (right-click Start → Terminal (Admin)).

Run this command:
```powershell
wsl --install
```

Wait for it to download and install Ubuntu. When it says to restart, restart your computer.

After restart, Ubuntu will open automatically. Create a **username** (lowercase, no spaces) and **password** (you won't see characters while typing — that's normal).

Verify by typing:
```bash
echo "Hello from Linux!"
```

steps.title: Navigate the File System
steps.instructions:
Try these commands one by one:

```bash
# Where am I?
pwd

# What's here?
ls

# Show hidden files too
ls -la

# Go to the root of the entire system
cd /
ls

# Go back home
cd ~

# Access your Windows files
ls /mnt/c/Users/

# See your Windows Desktop from Linux!
ls /mnt/c/Users/$USER/Desktop/ 2>/dev/null || ls /mnt/c/Users/*/Desktop/
```

Notice: Linux uses `/` (forward slash), not `\` (backslash) like Windows.

steps.title: Create a Project Structure
steps.instructions:
Build a web project folder using only terminal commands:

```bash
# Create the project with nested folders in one command
mkdir -p ~/my-website/{css,js,images,pages}

# Create files
touch ~/my-website/index.html
touch ~/my-website/css/style.css
touch ~/my-website/js/app.js
touch ~/my-website/pages/about.html
touch ~/my-website/pages/contact.html
touch ~/my-website/.gitignore

# See what you built
sudo apt install tree -y
tree ~/my-website/
```

You should see a nice tree structure. Screenshot this output.

steps.title: Work with Files
steps.instructions:
```bash # Write content to a file echo '' > ~/my-website/index.html echo '' >> ~/my-website/index.html echo 'My Website' >> ~/my-website/index.html echo '

Hello World

' >> ~/my-website/index.html echo '' >> ~/my-website/index.html # Read the file cat ~/my-website/index.html # Write CSS echo 'body { font-family: Arial; margin: 0; padding: 20px; }' > ~/my-website/css/style.css echo 'h1 { color: #6366f1; }' >> ~/my-website/css/style.css # Read it cat ~/my-website/css/style.css # Copy a file cp ~/my-website/index.html ~/my-website/index-backup.html # Rename a file mv ~/my-website/index-backup.html ~/my-website/backup.html # Delete the backup rm ~/my-website/backup.html # Verify it's gone ls ~/my-website/ ```

steps.title: Write Your First Script
steps.instructions:
Create a script that sets up any new project:

```bash
# Open nano editor
nano ~/setup-project.sh
```

Type this inside nano:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
echo "Enter project name:"
read PROJECT_NAME

mkdir -p ~/$PROJECT_NAME/{src,tests,docs}
touch ~/$PROJECT_NAME/README.md
touch ~/$PROJECT_NAME/.gitignore
echo "# $PROJECT_NAME" > ~/$PROJECT_NAME/README.md
echo "Created on: $(date)" >> ~/$PROJECT_NAME/README.md
echo "__pycache__/" > ~/$PROJECT_NAME/.gitignore
echo ".env" >> ~/$PROJECT_NAME/.gitignore

echo "Project '$PROJECT_NAME' created!"
tree ~/$PROJECT_NAME/
```

Save: **Ctrl+O** → Enter → **Ctrl+X**

Make it executable and run:
```bash
chmod +x ~/setup-project.sh
./setup-project.sh
```

Type a project name when prompted. Screenshot the output.

**Submit:** Screenshot of the tree output + the script file.
